headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Privy.io documentation spans 636 pages with 100% crawl coverage and strong structural foundations: zero broken repository links, 100% evidence coverage on 636 detected claims, and 100% answerability/citationability for retrieval. Critical gaps include 5 confirmed broken internal docs links, 19.61% SEO/geo issue rate, 61.57% API reference coverage across 269 detected API pages, and near-zero freshness visibility (1.1% last-updated coverage). Example reliability shows 0% detection across all pages, flagged as likely JS-rendering limitation rather than true absence. Overall retrieval readiness scores 70.97 (moderate band), constrained by 71.76% stale-risk and 65.25% chunkability.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

priority_actions.title: Fix all 5 confirmed broken internal docs links
priority_actions.why_this_first: Immediate trust and navigation win affecting every user journey, zero repo links means all breaks are customer-facing, trivial effort for measurable UX gain.

priority_actions.title: Add last-updated timestamps to all 636 pages (currently 1.1% coverage, 7 pages)
priority_actions.why_this_first: Unlocks trust and reduces support burden by letting users self-assess currency, directly mitigates 71.76% stale-risk perception, and improves SEO freshness signals.

priority_actions.title: Close API reference coverage gap from 61.57% to 85%+ by documenting missing endpoints across 269 API pages
priority_actions.why_this_first: Developer onboarding and time-to-value depend on complete API docs; 38% gap creates friction, support tickets, and churn risk for technical users.

strengths: Complete crawl coverage (100.16%) with 636 pages discovered and indexed, zero repository navigation link breakage
100% evidence coverage: all 636 key claims detected are supported by evidence
100% answerability and citationability scores ensure strong AI retrieval and attribution potential
risks: 5 confirmed broken internal docs links degrade user navigation and trust, all user-facing (0 repo links broken)
19.61% SEO/geo issue rate threatens organic discoverability and search ranking for ~125 pages
61.57% API reference coverage leaves 38% of API surface undocumented across 269 detected API pages, risking developer onboarding friction
0% example reliability detection across 636 pages suggests JS-rendered code blocks invisible to crawlers and LLM training pipelines
limitations: External audit cannot verify actual code example correctness, version compatibility, or runnability; 0% detection rate indicates JS-rendered samples invisible to crawler, so true quality remains unassessed.
Crawl-based analysis cannot assess gated content, authenticated API docs, or dynamic user-specific documentation paths not discoverable via public sitemap and links.
Audit measures structural signals (chunkability, citationability) but cannot guarantee semantic accuracy, technical correctness, or alignment with current product behavior.
automation_first: Deploy automated link checker running weekly to catch broken internal links before users do; 5 confirmed breaks found in this audit, preventing recurring navigation failures and trust erosion with <1 hour setup using existing CI/CD.

Auto-inject last-updated timestamps via build pipeline or CMS hook to lift 1.1% coverage (7 pages) to 100%, directly reducing 71.76% stale-risk perception and cutting support 'is this current?' inquiries with zero ongoing manual effort.

Integrate OpenAPI spec diff monitoring to alert on undocumented endpoints as API surface grows; current 61.57% coverage (269 pages, 38% gap) will drift further without automation, preventing silent documentation debt and developer friction.
